_what: Which licence covers which part of this repository, declared rather than described. The README says the same thing in prose; this file is the version a check can hold the tree to.
_rule: Every tracked top-level entry is either claimed by an area, listed in not_content, or listed in not_mine with a reason. Nothing may sit in this tree unlicensed and unexplained. Enforced by check N in code/check_published.py, in both directions: an area naming a path that does not exist fails too.
_why_two_way: The prose section in the README was correct and incomplete: it named code/, data/ and the two report pages, and said nothing about measurements/ -- 337 files including every artifact an outside reader would quote. Nobody noticed for weeks, because prose has no failing state. A declaration does.

areas.note: the programs. Permissive on purpose: the whole invitation is 'check it before believing any of it', and a reader should not need legal review to run the verifier.
the measurements and the declarations about them. Attribution is the only condition.
the report pages, the notes and the page assets. Same terms as the data.
the pre-registrations. Same terms; they are the part most worth quoting against, since they state what would falsify a figure before it was measured.

not_mine.why: a verbatim snapshot of the issuer's own public asset feed, archived so a figure derived from it can be rechecked later. It is not my content and I do not relicense it; its own terms apply. It is kept because a measurement that cites a feed and cannot show what the feed said is not recheckable.

verbatim endpoint responses, archived with digests so a reader can confirm what was read. These are records of public chain state rather than authored content; the CC-BY grant above covers my selection, arrangement and the records around them, not any claim over the chain's own bytes.
